archimate:Outcome.name: Faster Outbreak Detection and Reduced Public Health Risk
archimate:Outcome.documentation:
Faster Outbreak Detection and Reduced Public Health Risk is a proactive public health strategy achieved through the integration of real-time digital surveillance and automated diagnostic tracking.
Its primary purpose is to shrink the critical window between the initial emergence of a pathogen and the implementation of control measures, thereby preventing localized clusters from exploding into widespread epidemics.
Example: By linking hospital emergency room data directly to a centralized surveillance network, health officials can detect a sudden, anomalous spike in foodborne illness within hours, allowing them to pull contaminated produce from grocery store shelves before hundreds more people are exposed.
